question: Who was the first Governor General of Bengal ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Warren Hastings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Warren Hastings served as the first Governor-General of Bengal from 1773 to 1785.
 
• He was appointed under the Regulating Act of 1773, which was the first step towards central administration in India.
 
• Hastings played a crucial role in the consolidation of British power in India during the early years of colonial rule.
 
• His tenure was marked by administrative reforms, including the reorganization of revenue collection and the judicial system.
 
• Warren Hastings' governance laid the foundation for subsequent British policies in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act of 1773:**

 
 
• This was the first act passed by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of parliamentary control over the Company's administration in India.
 
• The Act established the position of Governor-General of Bengal along with an Executive Council of four members to assist him.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Reforms:**
 
 
• Hastings introduced judicial reforms, including the establishment of civil and criminal courts.
 
• He aimed to standardize revenue collection procedures and reduce corruption.
 
• His efforts were directed towards creating a more efficient and centralized administrative framework.
 
 
 
• **Anglo-Mysore Wars:**
 
 
• During Hastings' tenure, the First and Second Anglo-Mysore Wars were fought between the British East India Company and the Kingdom of Mysore.
 
• These conflicts were significant in expanding British influence in southern India.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Hastings' policies and administrative measures set the groundwork for future British governance in India.
 
• Despite controversies and impeachment trials in Britain, his contributions to the establishment of British rule are acknowledged by historians.
